title: Knowledge Check 6 - Lessons 26-30
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 26-30 - Practical Application of Agentforce Sales Expertise | Data Management. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Which feature applies a different exchange rate for different date ranges so converted opportunity amounts match the rate in effect when the deal was recorded?
options: Standard multi-currency conversion using the current active rate
Advanced Currency Management with dated exchange rates
A user's personal currency setting
The corporate currency setting alone
questions.explanation: Dated exchange rates under Advanced Currency Management bind each converted amount to the rate in effect on its date, while the standard conversion uses the current active rate and drifts retroactively.

questions.question: A rep syncs a quote to its opportunity. What happens to the opportunity products and Amount?
options: The opportunity products are copied up to the quote and the quote changes
Nothing changes until the opportunity is closed
The quote's line items are copied onto the opportunity's line items, overwriting its products, and the opportunity Amount updates from them
Only the opportunity contacts are updated from the quote
questions.explanation: Quote sync flows from the quote to the opportunity, overwriting the opportunity's line items and recomputing the Amount, so any prior manual edit to those lines is lost.

questions.question: An org has multiple currencies enabled. Which statement about a single opportunity is true?
options: One opportunity can hold products priced in several currencies at once
The corporate currency is set separately for each user
A single quote can mix currencies within its line items
A single opportunity uses exactly one currency, and every price book entry for its products must be in that same currency
questions.explanation: An opportunity transacts in exactly one currency and its price book entries must match it, so a product priced in another currency has no entry to bind to on that deal.

questions.question: Which object connects a lead or a contact to a campaign so you can track the person's response and measure return?
options: CampaignMember
Campaign
Lead
Opportunity
questions.explanation: CampaignMember is the join between a person and a campaign and it carries the member status that records the response, so a campaign with no members has nothing to measure.

questions.question: A web form must create leads and route them automatically to the right team by region. What does the routing?
options: A validation rule on the Lead object
A campaign influence model on the opportunity
Lead assignment rules that use ordered criteria, paired with the web-to-lead form
A price book entry on the lead's product
questions.explanation: Web-to-lead creates the lead and lead assignment rules route it by ordered criteria to a user or a queue, first matching rule winning, so the form and the rules work as a pair.

questions.question: After a lead is converted into an account, contact, and opportunity, what happens to the original lead record?
options: It is deleted once the opportunity is created
It becomes the opportunity and loses its lead fields
It is merged into the campaign that sourced it
It becomes read-only, its status is set to Converted, and it keeps the ids of the account, contact, and opportunity it created
questions.explanation: The lead is not removed; it becomes read-only, its status is set to Converted, and it retains the account, contact, and opportunity ids, which is how source attribution survives after conversion.

questions.question: Two sales teams follow different stage names and different win criteria on the same Opportunity object. What do you configure?
options: A single sales process with every stage both teams use
Two opportunity record types, each mapped to its own sales process
A validation rule that hides stage names per team
A campaign influence model per stage
questions.explanation: A sales process is bound to a record type, so two motions with different stages and win criteria need two record types each mapped to its own sales process, which also limits each record's stage picklist to that process.

questions.question: Reps updated stages faithfully but the forecast is still wrong. What most likely explains it?
options: The opportunity amounts were never converted to the corporate currency
The reps used the wrong campaign influence model
The opportunity team members were not added
A stage is mapped to the wrong forecast category, and the forecast is driven by forecast category, not the stage name
questions.explanation: The forecast reads the forecast category a stage maps to, so a faithful stage update still misstates the forecast when the stage-to-category mapping is wrong.

questions.question: A solutions engineer and an account executive both need forecast credit on the same deal. Which construct provides it?
options: Opportunity splits with split types that feed split forecasts
Contact roles on the opportunity
Campaign members on the sourcing campaign
Extra price book entries for the deal
questions.explanation: OpportunitySplit records divide revenue or overlay credit by percentage across contributors and can feed split forecasts, while contact roles name the customer side and campaign members measure marketing response.

questions.question: A customer keeps their ERP as the source of truth for orders but wants Salesforce to show the same orders to the sales team, with updates flowing both ways every day. Is this a migration or an integration, and why?
options: A migration, because the data has to be moved into Salesforce
An integration, because both systems stay live and both keep changing the data
A migration followed by a one time cleanup
Neither, because the ERP cannot connect to Salesforce
questions.explanation: Both systems remain systems of record and keep changing, so the work is ongoing synchronization, which is an integration rather than a one time migration.

questions.question: During planning for a migration of 40,000 accounts, the consultant finds thousands of duplicate accounts and records with country values that do not match the target picklist. What should happen before the production load?
options: Load everything and clean up in Salesforce afterward
Load only the accounts that pass validation and leave the rest behind
Deduplicate and normalize the values in the source, then validate with a test load in a full sandbox
Import with the Data Import Wizard to force validation rules to fix the values
questions.explanation: Cleansing and deduplicating in the source is far cheaper than fixing records after they land in Salesforce, and a full sandbox test load proves the mapping and the counts first.

questions.question: The migration team wants to confirm the load will finish inside a four hour maintenance window before they touch production. What is the correct approach?
options: Run a test load with representative data volumes in a full copy sandbox and measure the run time
Estimate the time by dividing the record count by the API limit
Load directly into production during off hours since it is the only real environment
Ask Salesforce Support to raise the governor limits for the load
questions.explanation: Only a full copy sandbox mirrors production closely enough to produce a credible run time, so a measured test load there is the way to validate the window.

questions.question: An admin must import 120,000 Contacts reliably and repeatably, and the target object supports the API. Which tool fits?
options: Data Import Wizard, because it enforces validation rules
The Data Import Wizard in several runs, since it is the safest option
Data Loader, because it handles up to 5 million records while the Data Import Wizard stops at 50,000
A manual paste into the UI list view
questions.explanation: 120,000 exceeds the Data Import Wizard's 50,000 record limit, and Data Loader's larger ceiling and object coverage make it the tool for the volume. Duplicate rules apply to both tools, so duplicate handling is not what decides the tool.

questions.question: A migration package contains Opportunities, Accounts, Contacts, Products, and Opportunity Line Items. Which load order is correct?
options: Opportunities, then Accounts, then Contacts, then Products, then Line Items
Accounts, then Contacts, then Opportunities, then Products, then Opportunity Line Items
Contacts, then Accounts, then Products, then Line Items, then Opportunities
Line Items first, because they carry the most detail
questions.explanation: Parents must exist before the children that reference them, and Opportunity Line Items depend on Price Book Entries, which depend on Products and Price Books, so the parent to child order is the only one that resolves.

questions.question: A nightly upsert job fails halfway, and the team wants to rerun it without creating duplicate Contacts. What makes the rerun safe?
options: Deleting all the loaded records before rerunning
Running an upsert that matches on the external ID field, so existing rows update instead of inserting again
Switching to insert and hoping the duplicates are few
Enabling duplicate rules and letting them block the second run
questions.explanation: Upsert matches incoming rows on the external ID, so a rerun updates the records that already landed and only inserts the rows that never made it, which is what makes an incremental load re runnable.
